newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Mubarak in Tripoli for talks with Gaddafi.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak in Tripoli for talks with Gaddafi.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak arrived in Tripoli on Monday for talks with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported.
Mubarak was welcomed at Tripoli's airport by Gaddafi and senior Libyan officials, said the agency, received in Tunis.
"We will have exchanges over issues interesting the region and on boosting relations between Egypt and Libya," JANA quoted Mubarak as saying on arrival.
He said that talks on bilateral issues will include cooperation in the fields of electrictity and railway connections.
"The visit came as Libya and Egypt were coordinating their positions on the intervention force in southern Mediterranean some European countries have set up," JANA said.

Gaddafi has branded as "international terrorism" a decision by Italy, France, Spain and Portugal to have a joint force that could be used for humanitarian and peacekeeping crises, such as the one now engulfing eastern Zaire.
Security sources at the Egyptian-Libyan border earlier said Mubarak drove his own car across the border to the eastern Libyan town of Tobruk where he took a plane to the capital Tripoli.

A U.N. air embargo bans air travel to or from Libya. The travel restrictions are aimed at forcing Libya to hand over two of its citizens wanted for the bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Scotland in 1988.
Mubarak's talks with Gaddafi were expected to cover joint cooperation projects and general Arab issues, the sources said.
The Egyptian president is expected to spend the night in Libya and return home on Tuesday, the Egyptian sources said.
Tight security was imposed on a camp for Palestinian refugees on the Egyptian-Libyan border to prevent the inhabitants from staging a protest, the sources said.
The camp is next to the main road that connects the two countries.
The refugees have been stranded in the camp since September 1995 when Gaddafi expelled thousands of Palestinians in a bid to show the futility of the Palestinian Authority's peace deal with Israel.

Many Palestinians have since returned to the Palestinian self-rule areas. Egypt has refused to allow any of them in unless they have travel documents to other countries. It has made a few exceptions in cases of medical emergencies.
